content.thinking:
This intervention personalizes climate scientists by highlighting their warmth and community ties, which should meaningfully boost trust—particularly on benevolence dimensions—though likely with smaller spillover effects on belief, concern, and policy support. Given that trust in climate scientists already sits fairly high in the US (~65-70), I'm factoring in ceiling effects when estimating the likely magnitude, probably landing in the 2-4 point range typical of effective narrative megastudy interventions.

I'm now working through estimates across all the outcome measures—trust variants, distrust, funding perceptions, policy role and general/specific policy support, institutional trust, belief, concern, behavior, and the small-stakes donation and newsletter signup items—weighing which ones the emotionally resonant, non-partisan, benevolence-focused narrative would move most versus least.

I therefore expect it to be among the better-performing arms on the primary multidimensional trust measure (especially benevolence), but constrained by high baseline trust (~65–70/100) and ceiling effects, so a few points at most. The single-item trust and belief measures are pre-measured, so anchoring shrinks movement roughly by half relative to the fresh multidimensional battery; distrust items are stickier and move less in absolute magnitude.
